\paragraph{Notation.}   The Bregman divergence associated with $f$ is the mapping $$D_{f} (x, y) \; \eqdef \; f(x) - f(y) - \ev{ \nabla f(y), x - y }, \quad x,y\in R^d$$ and the proximal operator of $\gamma R$ is the function $$\prox_{\gamma R} \br{x} \; \eqdef \; \argmin_u \left\{ \gamma R(x) + \frac{1}{2} \norm{x-u}^2\right\}.$$ Let $[n] \eqdef \left\{1,\dots,n\right\}$.

\begin{proof}
    Because $x_\ast$ is a minimizer of $F$ we have that $- \nabla f(x_\ast)  \in \partial R(x_\ast)$. By the definition of subgradients we have
    \[ R(x_\ast) + \ev{ - \nabla f(x_\ast), x - x_\ast } \leq R(x). \]
    Rearranging gives
    \[ -\ev{ \nabla f(x_\ast), x - x_\ast} \leq R(x) - R(x_\ast) \]
    Adding $f(x) - f(x_\ast)$ to both sides we have,
    \[ f(x) - f(x_\ast) - \ev{ \nabla f(x_\ast), x - x_\ast } \leq f(x) + R(x) - \br{ f(x_\ast) + R(x_\ast)} = F(x) - F(x_\ast). \]
   Now note that the on the left hand side we have the Bregman divergence $D_{f} (x, x_\ast)$.
\end{proof}

nodes.title: 引用经典第二近端定理

declaration_text: Second Prox Theorem, cited from Beck (2017), Section 6.5: if h is proper, lower semicontinuous and convex, gamma > 0, and p = prox_{gamma h}(y), then h(p)-h(z) <= -(1/gamma)<p-y,p-z> for every z in dom(h).

nodes.title: 近端算子非扩张性
declaration_text: For a proper lower semicontinuous convex h and gamma > 0, ||prox_{gamma h}(u)-prox_{gamma h}(v)|| <= ||u-v||.

nodes.title: 条件方差恒等式
declaration_text: For a square-integrable random vector X and sigma-algebra G, E[||X-E[X|G]||^2|G] = E[||X||^2|G]-||E[X|G]||^2 <= E[||X||^2|G].

nodes.title: 凸最优性与次梯度定义
declaration_text: For differentiable convex f and convex R, a minimizer x_* of f+R satisfies -grad f(x_*) in partial R(x_*). If s in partial R(x_*), then R(x) >= R(x_*)+<s,x-x_*> for every x.

nodes.title: 凸函数詹森不等式
declaration_text: If F is convex, w_k >= 0 and sum_k w_k = 1, then F(sum_k w_k x_k) <= sum_k w_k F(x_k).

nodes.title: 条件期望塔式法则
declaration_text: For integrable X and a sigma-algebra G, E[E[X|G]] = E[X]; expectation is linear over finite integrable sums.
